title: finding(ci): objectui's labeler runs on every push with `sync-labels: true` and its own comment says it writes the whole set in ONE `setLabels` call — if that reading holds, a hand-hung `needs:contract-review` carrier does not survive the next push
body:
Surfaced by the `os-dev` lane delivering PR objectui#9864 (card objectui#8157), which flagged it as an open question rather than acting on it, and **re-measured by the reviewing seat**. ⛔ Filed as an **unmeasured hazard with the experiment named**, ⛔ not as a confirmed defect — see «What is NOT measured», which is the load-bearing half.

## The hazard

`needs:contract-review` is the clause-② gate's **PR-side carrier**: `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair` refuses a pair (exit 4, C1) when the card carries it and the PR does not — 「the pair was written half way」. A PM seat hangs it by hand.

Measured on `origin/main`:

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/labeler.yml` trigger | `on: pull_request` · `types: [opened, **synchronize**, reopened]` ⇒ runs on **every push**, not only at open |
| the action | `actions/labeler@v7` with **`sync-labels: true`** |
| ⭐ the workflow's OWN comment, `:18`–`:21` | *"The action applies the whole set in **ONE `setLabels` call**"* |
| `.github/labeler.yml` declares `needs:contract-review` | **0** |
| `.github/labeler.yml` declares any `pm:` label | **0** |

⇒ **if** the whole label set is replaced on each push with the labeler's computed set, a hand-hung `needs:contract-review` does not survive the next push — and the pair goes half-written with **nobody having touched it**. That is the exact shape `check-clause2-carriers` was built to catch, arriving by a route no seat can be blamed for.

## ⛔ What is NOT measured — and why the card stops here

**Two readings are live and I did not distinguish them:**

1. The repo's own comment says `setLabels`, which replaces the full set ⇒ an unmanaged label is dropped.
2. `actions/labeler` v5+ is documented to remove only labels its **own configuration manages** that no longer match ⇒ a label absent from the config is left alone, and the carrier survives.

⛔ I have **no natural experiment** in today's history to tell them apart: on every clause-②-`yes` PR this shift the carrier was hung **after** the last push, so none of them was ever pushed to while hung.

⭐ **The experiment is cheap and should be run before anyone acts**: take any open PR, add a label absent from `.github/labeler.yml`, push one commit to it, and read the label set back. One push answers it.

## Why it is worth a card even unmeasured

If reading 1 holds, **every clause-②-`yes` PR in this repository is one push away from a half-written pair**, and the failure is silent, mechanical and blameless — the seat did its job, the workflow undid it. That is a gate whose carrier the repo's own CI removes.

⚠️ And the cost is asymmetric: reading 2 costs nothing to assume and is wrong half the time; reading 1 costs a re-hang nobody knows is owed. ⇒ the reading has to be taken, not guessed.

## Adjacent, and it is the reason the lane raised it

A standing dev-side clause budgets a `POST /issues/{n}/labels` as the seat's own step. In objectui that is at best inert and at worst harmful, and the clause's **own hazard note** — a whole-set write erasing a correct additive one — describes this workflow exactly. ⇒ the reviewing seat ruled **do not hand-apply labels on an objectui PR**; the labeler applies `plugin`, `tests`, `package: *` and friends on its own. ⛔ That ruling does **not** extend to `needs:contract-review`, which no labeler rule supplies and which the gate requires — which is precisely why the interaction above needs settling rather than a convention.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether any historical PR in this repo lost a hand-applied label at a push — no timeline scan was run. ⛔ Whether the `issues: write` permission the workflow carries changes the call shape. ⛔ Whether the sibling repository's labeler has the same configuration.

Refs: objectui#8157 / PR objectui#9864 (the delivery that raised it) · `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` (the gate whose carrier this is) · objectstack#18885 (the open conflict about clause-② review routing — ⛔ a different question about the same gate).
